Package frc.robot.aiming

Class PhysicsAim

java.lang.Object
frc.robot.aiming.PhysicsAim
All Implemented Interfaces:
AimStrategy
public class PhysicsAim extends Object implements AimStrategy
Ballistic trajectory solver that computes shooter angle and speed from first-principles kinematics, taking robot motion into account.

Unlike ToFAim, which fits a polynomial to empirical calibration data, PhysicsAim derives launch parameters analytically from the 3D offset between the shooter and the target.

Algorithm overview

  1. The ball must arrive at the target with a specific downward velocity. The range of acceptable descent speeds (minDescentVelocity to maxDescentVelocity) defines the family of valid trajectories â€” a shallow arc at min speed, a steep arc at max speed.
  2. quicksolve(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation3d, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d, double) analytically finds launch velocity for any given descent speed using a quadratic equation derived from projectile-motion equations.
  3. update(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Pose3d, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Pose3d, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d) first tries the minimum (lowest-energy) trajectory. If that satisfies AimConstraints, it returns immediately. Otherwise it binary-searches the descent-speed range across ITERATIONS iterations to find the shallowest trajectory that still satisfies the constraints.
  4. A final yaw sanity check rejects any solution whose computed launch direction differs from the actual direction to the target by more than 0.8 Ï€ radians (144Â°). Such solutions are mathematically valid but physically impossible â€” the shooter cannot reach the target in that direction.

  • Method Details

    • update

      public AimParams update(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Pose3d target, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Pose3d shooter, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d shooterVelocity)
      Computes the optimal launch parameters to reach target from shooter.

      The method first attempts the minimum-descent-speed (flattest) trajectory, which requires the least projectile speed. If the flat trajectory violates AimConstraints, it binary-searches the descent-speed range to find the shallowest feasible arc.

      Returns AimParams.impossible() when no trajectory within the descent-speed range can satisfy the constraints, or when the computed yaw deviates more than 144Â° from the straight-line direction to the target.

      Specified by:
      update in interface AimStrategy
      Parameters:
      target - 3D pose of the scoring target (hub opening center).
      shooter - 3D pose of the shooter exit point.
      shooterVelocity - Field-relative robot velocity at the shooter (m/s in x and y). Subtracted from projectile velocity so the ball travels to the target regardless of robot motion.
      Returns:
      Launch parameters (AimParams), or AimParams.impossible() if no feasible solution exists.

    • quicksolve

      public static AimParams quicksolve(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation3d offset, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Translation2d robotVelocity, double finalDescentSpeed)
      Analytically solves for launch velocity given a fixed terminal descent speed.

      Derivation

      We require it to descend at finalDescentSpeed on arrival, so:

      Substituting into the height equation and rearranging:

      This is the quadratic aÂ·tÂ² + bÂ·t + c = 0 with a = Â½g, b = âˆ’finalDescentSpeed, c = âˆ’dz. We take the positive root for a physically meaningful (forward-in-time) solution.

      With flight time known, horizontal velocities follow from uniform motion: vx = dx/t, vy = dy/t. Robot velocity is subtracted so the ball travels to the target regardless of whether the robot is moving.

      Parameters:
      offset - Vector from shooter to target (meters: x forward, y left, z up).
      robotVelocity - Field-relative robot velocity in the horizontal plane (m/s).
      finalDescentSpeed - Desired downward speed (m/s, positive = downward) at impact.
